evals.prompt: Build a portfolio site for our hackathon project DispatchAI, an empathetic AI 911 dispatcher. It won Grand Prize at the UC Berkeley AI Hackathon (1 of 293 submissions). Stack is Next.js, FastAPI, a fine-tuned Mistral-7B, Retell, and Hume. Demo is at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hdpdgxrilQM. I want recruiters to take it seriously.
evals.expected_output: A one-page, recruiter-facing case-study site with a project-specific design produced via the frontend-design skill, covering hero, credibility, problem, what it does, architecture, an interactive or embedded showcase, results, team, and honest limits.
expectations: The skill installs or confirms Anthropic's frontend-design skill before designing, and derives a palette and type system from the project rather than a template.
The plan includes an embedded/interactive or seeded showcase for the web app plus the demo video, not just screenshots.
No awards or stats are invented beyond those provided, and an 'honest limits' section is included.

evals.prompt: I need a portfolio website for my hackathon project, but it's not a web app. It's a hardware bike-tracking mesh network (Arduino + LoRa radios + a Firestore backend). Built by 4 students in 36 hours. We placed Top 10 globally. There's no live app to click. Read the repo for the rest.
evals.expected_output: A recruiter-facing case-study site that showcases a non-web-app project through photos, a system diagram, field footage, and a telemetry or map replay, with a distinctive design from the frontend-design skill.
expectations: The skill recognizes the project is not a web app and chooses hardware-appropriate showcase devices (build photos, wiring/system diagram, field footage, map or telemetry replay) instead of an embedded live app.
It still produces a unique design via frontend-design and reads the repo before asking for missing facts.
The site remains recruiter-first with credibility, architecture, by-the-numbers, team, and links sections, and invents no awards or metrics.
